en.headline: Residents join free Sport For All Day activities across the city
en.dek: The Leisure and Cultural Services Department offered free access to facilities and programmes on Sunday under the theme Asian Games in Motion, City in Action, with Chief Executive John Lee among participants.
body: Hong Kong residents turned out in numbers on Sunday for Sport For All Day, with designated leisure facilities and sports programmes open free of charge across all 18 districts.

The Leisure and Cultural Services Department organised the annual event under the theme “Asian Games in Motion, City in Action” to mark the approaching 20th Asian Games in September and encourage public support for Hong Kong athletes. Free sports and recreation programmes ran from 2 pm to 6 pm at designated venues, while a wide range of LCSD facilities were available without charge over the weekend.

Chief Executive John Lee attended and later wrote on social media that the activities were diversified, covering both conventional and emerging sports. He called on the public to support the city’s athletes at the Games.

Participants included families trying handball, rowing, football and other activities. One father who brought his daughter to Kowloon Park Sports Centre said they wanted to experience several sports, while a young participant noted that such events help people understand their fitness levels and support physical and mental health.

zh.headline: 市民踴躍參與全民運動日免費活動
zh.dek: 康文署周日以「亞運動起來 全城動起來」為主題，全港18區指定場地提供免費設施及體育活動，行政長官李家超亦有出席。
body: 本港市民周日踴躍參與全民運動日，全港18區指定康樂設施及體育活動免費開放，吸引不少家庭到場體驗。
康樂及文化事務署以「亞運動起來 全城動起來」為主題舉辦一年一度活動，配合九月舉行的第20屆亞洲運動會，呼籲市民支持香港運動員。指定場地由下午2時至6時提供免費體育及康樂活動，周末多項康文署設施亦免費使用。
行政長官李家超到場參與，其後在社交平台表示活動多元化，涵蓋傳統及新興運動，並呼籲市民為即將參賽的港隊健兒加油。
市民包括帶同女兒到九龍公園體育館的父親，表示想體驗手球、划艇及足球等項目；一名少年則指活動可讓人了解自身體能，並有助身心健康。
